text:
patrick: FYI - onboarding quickstart in samples crashes on first run after we bumped Kotlin SDK -> OkHttp 4.12. Stacktrace points to NoSuchMethodError on okhttp3.internal.platform.Platform.get(). Happening when minifyEnabled = true in sample's release build.

jen: log?

patrick: pasted minimal stack: 
```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: No static method get()Lokhttp3/internal/platform/Platform; in class Lokhttp3/internal/platform/Platform; or its super classes (declaration of 'okhttp3.internal.platform.Platform' appears in /data/app/.../base.apk)
  at okhttp3.OkHttpClient$Builder.build(OkHttpClient.java:XXX)
  at com.redwood.sample.NetworkModule.provideOkHttp(NetworkModule.kt:42)
  ...
```

miguel: that screams R8/ProGuard stripping something used reflectively. OkHttp uses internal Platform reflection for TLS/platform adapters. Normally OkHttp ships consumer ProGuard rules so consumers shouldn't need to add anything, but sample's Gradle config might be overriding consumer rules or using "minifyEnabled true" without the proper proguardFiles.

jen: sample quickstart is meant for new users; this is a big onboarding friction if the release build (minified) crashes out-of-the-box.

miguel: quick fixes: 1) ensure consumer proguard files are merged (check packagingOptions and consumerProguardFiles in Gradle), 2) add explicit keep rule in sample app until we diagnose root cause:

```
# keep OkHttp internal platform helpers used via reflection
-keep class okhttp3.internal.platform.Platform { *; }
-keep class okhttp3.internal.tls.TrustRootIndex { *; }
```

Also recommend disabling minify in the sample quickstart releaseVariant for now: `minifyEnabled false` so users don't hit this.

patrick: I'm worried about recommending disabling minify in general, but for the sample app that's fine. We should also check if our SDK aar shading step accidentally strips consumer rules when repackaging.

jen: priority: add short runbook and docs blurb in the quickstart README: "If your release build crashes with NoSuchMethodError in OkHttp, try disabling minify or add keep rules. We'll include the recommended proguard snippet."

docs-bot: doc task created: DOCS-789 add proguard troubleshooting to Kotlin SDK quickstart.

miguel: also add a CI smoke: build the sample with `minifyEnabled true` and run basic startup test on emulator to catch regressions. Add that as a flaky-guard so we catch future OkHttp upgrades.

patrick: opened PR with two commits: 1) change sample build variant to minifyEnabled false + README note, 2) add a repro branch and a small proguard snippet (commented) we can toggle. Tests added: simple start + network warmup on emulator in CI. PR number in repo: 6342.

build-bot: CI started for PR #6342 on branch `sample-proguard-fix`.

jen: once PR lands, please add a short blurb in the SDK release notes about "If you encounter NoSuchMethodError after OkHttp bump, follow quickstart proguard troubleshooting". This will reduce support tickets.

patrick: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:

---
Notes: Repro steps included in PR: 1) enable minifyEnabled true in samples/app/build.gradle, 2) build release apk, 3) install on API 29 emulator, 4) open app -> crash on network init. Workaround: disable minify or add keep rules above. We'll follow up to find why consumer rules didn't apply in our sample packaging step.
